ai.description: This skink reaches 8 cm SVL. It is bronze-brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe and pale spots. Key features include heavily keeled dorsal scales and a white-edged ear opening.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis rugifera* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of three distinct, strongly keeled scales on each dorsal row, giving the body a noticeably rough texture.
ai.habitat: The Rough-scaled Sun Skink inhabits moist, shaded forest floors and leaf litter within tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Rough-scaled Sun Skink is primarily diurnal and actively hunts small invertebrates among leaf litter, often retreating into crevices or burrows when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis rugifera* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, spanning from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis rugifera* is found in the Western Ghats of India, specifically in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
